claims.text: AlCrFeNiSi is a cobalt-free high-entropy alloy that can be processed from powder feedstock.
Conventional additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi typically produces rapid-cooling-induced compositional segregation.
Conventional additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi typically produces high residual thermal stresses.
Conventional additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi typically produces notable defects.
Build-plate preheating reduces the thermal gradients during additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi.
A machine-learning model using real-time thermal feedback can continuously optimize the build-plate preheat temperature.
A more uniform melt-pool and surrounding temperature distribution limits elemental segregation during solidification.
Reduced thermal gradients alleviate residual thermal stresses in the fabricated alloy.
Reduced thermal gradients minimize microstructural defect formation.
Build-plate preheating decreases the temperature differential between the melt pool and the substrate.
The decreased melt-pool-to-substrate temperature differential slows the cooling rate.
Slower cooling promotes more homogeneous solidification.
Real-time preheat optimization adapts to process variations and reduces stress concentrations and defects.
ML-optimized build-plate preheating will improve the mechanical integrity of additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi relative to a room-temperature build plate.
ML-optimized build-plate preheating will reduce compositional segregation, residual stress, and defect density relative to the baseline.
ML-optimized build-plate preheating will increase tensile strength relative to the baseline.
ML-optimized build-plate preheating will increase ductility relative to the baseline.
Laser powder bed fusion has been used to fabricate high-entropy or concentrated alloys.
The proposed intervention is expected to hold in laser powder bed fusion or comparable rapid-solidification additive-manufacturing processes.
Prior additive-manufacturing trends and thermal-management principles make the proposed mechanism plausible.
